subject: physics
question_text: State the parallelogram law of vectors. Derive an expression for the magnitude and direction of the resultant vector.

verification.note: Two cuts ship: LAQ/8 (Section C, from the TSBIE Basic Learning Material) and SAQ/4 (Section B, from the Sri Chaitanya Fastrack, which lists this as SHORT ANSWER 1 of Unit 4 and has no LONG ANSWER section at all). The sources disagree on the section, so the student can switch. BOTH mark splits, and the choice of which steps the 4-mark answer omits, are claims until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms them. Star rank is the book’s; no exam appearance years are printed for Unit 4, so appearances[] stays empty.

steps.label: State the law
steps.margin_note: Write the whole statement. The two marks are for the words alone.
lines: If two vectors acting at a point are represented
in magnitude and direction by the two adjacent
sides of a parallelogram drawn from that point,
then their resultant is represented in magnitude
and direction by the diagonal of the parallelogram
drawn from the same point.

recall.must_convey: Both halves of the law: the two vectors at a point are the two adjacent sides of a parallelogram, AND the resultant is the diagonal from that same point. If only one half is spoken, not covered, confidence 0.5 or lower.
accept: two vectors as the two adjacent sides of a parallelogram then the resultant is the diagonal from the same point
if two vectors act at a point they are the sides of a parallelogram and the diagonal is the resultant
adjacent sides represent the two vectors and the diagonal represents the resultant in magnitude and direction
rendu vectors ni parallelogram lo adjacent sides ga theeskunte diagonal ye resultant
first the statement two vectors adjacent sides diagonal is the resultant
reject: the resultant is the sum of the two vectors

steps.why: The examiner gives two of the eight marks for the words alone, before any physics. Writing the full statement is the cheapest scoring you will do in this answer.
common_mistakes: Writing only half the law — the two adjacent sides, but not that the diagonal is the resultant.
Saying 'the resultant is the sum' instead of stating the law.
Leaving out 'drawn from the same point', so the diagonal is not pinned down.
steps.memory_tip: Remember the statement in two halves: the two vectors are two adjacent sides; the resultant is the diagonal from the same point.

steps.label: Draw the figure
steps.margin_note: Label every point: O, A, B, C, D. Mark the angles θ and α and the sides P, Q, R. One mark is for a complete, labelled figure.

recall.must_convey: That a figure is drawn at this point in the answer. Naming the act of drawing is full credit. The student cannot speak a diagram.
accept: then I draw the figure
diagram geestha
draw the parallelogram OACB
I draw a parallelogram with the two vectors as sides
picture veyali
reject: the diagonal of the parallelogram is the resultant

steps.why: Every later line names a point from this figure. Without it, the examiner cannot follow OD, CD or angle alpha, and the derivation marks become hard to award.
common_mistakes: Drawing the diagonal from the wrong corner of OACB.
Leaving points unlabelled, so later steps refer to nothing.
Forgetting to mark the angles theta and alpha.
steps.memory_tip: Draw before you derive: base P, slanted Q at angle θ, diagonal R. Drop the perpendicular CD at once.

steps.label: Construction
steps.margin_note: Name every point you drew. The examiner matches these names against the figure.
lines: Let OA = P and OB = Q act at the point O,
with ∠AOB = θ.
Complete the parallelogram OACB.
Join OC. The diagonal OC = R is the resultant.
Draw CD ⊥ to OA extended, meeting it at D.
Let ∠AOC = α.

recall.must_convey: That the construction is written after the figure. Saying the word construction is full credit. So is naming any part of it: OA = P, OB = Q, angle AOB = theta, complete OACB, join OC, drop CD perpendicular to OA extended, angle AOC = alpha.
accept: then construction
OA is P and OB is Q and the angle between them is theta
complete the parallelogram OACB and join OC
drop a perpendicular from C to OA extended
construction raastha

steps.why: This names what you drew so the algebra has something to attach to. The perpendicular CD is the whole trick of the proof: it turns the parallelogram into a right triangle.
common_mistakes: Dropping the perpendicular to OA instead of to OA extended.
Not saying which angle is theta and which is alpha.
steps.memory_tip: One line to remember: extend OA and drop CD perpendicular onto it. That right triangle is the whole plan.

steps.label: Find AD and CD
steps.margin_note: AC is parallel to OB, so the angle at A equals θ. Both legs come from this one triangle.
lines: In the right triangle CAD:

lines.text: ∴ OD = OA + AD = P + Q cos θ

recall.must_convey: The two legs from right triangle CAD. EITHER naming both legs AD = Q cos theta and CD = Q sin theta, OR naming OD = P + Q cos theta, is enough. Q resolved into a component along P and one perpendicular to P also counts.
accept: AD is Q cos theta and CD is Q sin theta
resolve Q into Q cos theta along OA and Q sin theta perpendicular
OD becomes P plus Q cos theta
in the triangle CAD the angle is theta so the sides are Q cos theta and Q sin theta
components vasthayi Q cos theta and Q sin theta

steps.why: Q is at an angle, so it cannot be added to P directly. Resolving it into Q cos theta along P and Q sin theta perpendicular to P turns the problem into ordinary right-triangle geometry.
common_mistakes: Swapping the two — writing AD = Q sin theta and CD = Q cos theta.
Forgetting that angle CAD equals theta because AC is parallel to OB.
Writing OD = Q cos theta and leaving out the P.
steps.memory_tip: AD and CD are cos and sin of the SAME angle: along the base Q cos θ, standing up Q sin θ.

steps.label: Apply Pythagoras
steps.margin_note: Show the expansion and the sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 step. Skipping it loses the mark.
lines: In the right triangle ODC:

lines.text: R² = (P + Q cos θ)² + (Q sin θ)²
R² = P² + 2PQ cos θ + Q²cos²θ + Q²sin²θ
R² = P² + Q² + 2PQ cos θ  (∵ sin²θ + cos²θ = 1)

recall.must_convey: EITHER the move (Pythagoras on triangle ODC, OC squared equals OD squared plus CD squared) OR the result (R equals root of P squared plus Q squared plus 2PQ cos theta). Either one alone is full credit.
accept: apply Pythagoras theorem in triangle ODC
OC square equals OD square plus CD square
R equals root of P square plus Q square plus two PQ cos theta
expand it and sin square plus cos square becomes one
pythagoras petti magnitude vasthundi

steps.why: Pythagoras only works in a right triangle, which is exactly why CD was dropped perpendicular in the construction. The cos squared plus sin squared step is what collapses the long expression into the standard formula.
common_mistakes: Writing R squared = P squared + Q squared + 2PQ, leaving out cos theta.
Skipping the expansion and jumping to the final formula — the examiner looks for the middle line.
Not using sin squared theta + cos squared theta = 1, so the answer never simplifies.
steps.memory_tip: OD = P + Q cos θ. Square OD and DC and add — that is the whole magnitude step.

steps.label: Direction of R
steps.margin_note: Use the same right triangle ODC. Say which side is opposite and which is adjacent to α.
lines: Direction: in the right triangle ODC,

lines.text: tan α = Q sin θ / (P + Q cos θ)

recall.must_convey: The tangent relation for direction: tan alpha = CD / OD, that is tan alpha = Q sin theta over P + Q cos theta. The inverse form spoken at step 7 contains this relation and counts here too.
accept: tan alpha equals CD by OD
tan alpha is Q sin theta over P plus Q cos theta
for the direction tan alpha equals opposite by adjacent
alpha equals tan inverse of Q sin theta by P plus Q cos theta
heard_as: Q sin theta by P plus Q cos theta

steps.why: The magnitude alone does not fix a vector. The same right triangle ODC that gave the magnitude also gives the direction, so no new construction is needed here.
common_mistakes: Measuring alpha from Q instead of from P.
Writing tan alpha = Q sin theta / P, leaving out the Q cos theta.
Assuming alpha is half of theta, which is only true when P and Q are equal.
steps.memory_tip: Direction always comes from tan α in the same triangle ODC: Q sin θ over P + Q cos θ.

steps.label: Final answer for α
steps.margin_note: Box both final answers. The examiner finds them in one glance.
lines: The angle α gives the direction of R with P.

lines.text: ∴ α = tan⁻¹ [ Q sin θ / (P + Q cos θ) ]

recall.must_convey: The final answer written as alpha itself: alpha = tan inverse of [Q sin theta / (P + Q cos theta)]. Saying only tan alpha = ... is step 6, not this step.
accept: alpha equals tan inverse of Q sin theta by P plus Q cos theta
so alpha is tan inverse of that
I box alpha equal to tan inverse
alpha ni tan inverse lo raastha
reject: tan alpha equals Q sin theta by P plus Q cos theta
heard_as: tan to the power minus one

steps.why: The question asks for the direction, so the answer must be alpha itself, not tan alpha. Boxing both final results lets the examiner find them in one glance.
common_mistakes: Stopping at tan alpha and never writing alpha = tan inverse.
Leaving the answer unboxed among the working.
steps.memory_tip: The answer is α itself — write α = tan⁻¹(…) and box R and α together.

steps.label: Special cases (extra)
steps.margin_note: Not asked. Write it only if time is left.

recall.must_convey: That the special cases are added at the end. Naming them is full credit. Any one of the three values also counts: theta = 0 gives P + Q, theta = 90 gives root P square plus Q square, theta = 180 gives P minus Q.
accept: then special cases
when theta is zero R is P plus Q
at ninety degrees it is root P square plus Q square
maximum when they are in the same direction and minimum when opposite
last lo special cases raastha

steps.why: These three cases are the fastest way to check your own formula. If theta = 0 does not give P + Q, something in your derivation is wrong.
common_mistakes: Writing these instead of the derivation — they carry no marks in this question.
steps.memory_tip: Check with θ = 0°, 90°, 180°: you must get P + Q, √(P² + Q²), P − Q. If θ = 0 fails, a sign slipped.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

cuts.label: 8-mark answer
cuts.note: TSBIE Basic Learning Material 2021-22 lists this in Unit 4. The 8-mark split is a claim.

cuts.label: 4-mark answer

s1_statement.margin_note: Write the whole statement. The mark is for the words alone.
s1_statement.why: The examiner gives one of the four marks for the words alone, before any physics. Writing the full statement is the cheapest scoring you will do in this answer.

s5_pythagoras.label: Magnitude of R
lines: Let OA = P and OB = Q act at the point O,
with ∠AOB = θ. Complete parallelogram OACB.
Join OC = R. Draw CD ⊥ to OA extended.

lines.text: AD = Q cos θ,   CD = Q sin θ
OD = OA + AD = P + Q cos θ

lines: In the right triangle ODC:

lines.text: R² = OD² + CD² = (P + Q cos θ)² + (Q sin θ)²
R² = P² + 2PQ cos θ + Q²(cos²θ + sin²θ)

s7_alpha.label: Direction of R
lines: Let ∠AOC = α, the angle R makes with P.
From the same right triangle ODC:

lines.text: tan α = CD / OD = Q sin θ / (P + Q cos θ)
∴ α = tan⁻¹ [ Q sin θ / (P + Q cos θ) ]

cuts.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024) lists this as SHORT ANSWER 1 of Unit 4, three-star. The 4-mark split AND the choice of which steps a 4-mark answer may omit are both invented here - no real IPE paper has been seen at 4 marks. A Telangana IPE teacher must confirm before this cut reaches a student.

insider_note: The statement and the figure together carry 3 of the 8 marks — write them before any algebra.
